title: Ben Johnson on Bears' victory over Eagles | Press Conference
headline: Case Keenum started and played efficiently in a 27-7 win. Caleb Williams' availability for next week is unresolved, and Tyson Bagent remains the No. 2 QB.
summary: Johnson was proud of how the team bounced back from its first loss the week before, saying the win reflected a good week of preparation. The Bears played their cleanest game of the season with only five penalties. The defense was extraordinary in the second half, and the three takeaways were huge after Philadelphia moved the ball on them in the first half. Johnson would not single out any defender and credited the coordinator's plan. The run game struggled early but improved late. Case Keenum went 24 of 34 for almost 252 yards and 2 touchdowns, leaning on the passing game and getting the ball out quickly while the line protected well. Johnson said Keenum earned the start over Tyson Bagent through the course of the week's practices, and that Bagent also needed quality reps with the new pass catchers. Asked if Keenum would start again if Caleb Williams can't go, Johnson committed to nothing and said the staff will discuss it. He also noted Cameron Lewis' hip injury ahead of a short week.

injuries.detail: Dealing with a hip injury; Johnson said they'll see how he and others progress on a short week.
Johnson gave no injury details, but questions assumed Williams might not be available next week, and Keenum started in his place.

signals.claim: Keenum started in place of Caleb Williams and played efficiently; his role next week will be decided by the staff.
signals.note: He had a strong game in a pass-heavy script (24/34, ~252 yards, 2 TD). He is a fill-in option if Williams is out again, which makes him a streaming QB and a boost for the pass catchers.
signals.quote: case came through. He played lights out.

signals.claim: Bagent was the No. 2 QB coming out of training camp but did not start; whether he plays next week depends on a staff discussion.
signals.note: Keenum was chosen over Bagent this week, but Johnson left the QB2 situation open if Williams stays out.
signals.quote: there was a reason why Tyson, uh, ended training camp is our number two quarterback.

signals.note: Johnson did not say whether Williams will be available next week, so his status is the key QB item to monitor.

signals.claim: Lewis' hip injury will be monitored through a short week.
signals.note: His availability is uncertain, and little is known about the severity of the injury.

topics.detail: The ground game struggled for the first three quarters and only got going late. Johnson said he stuck with it and credited the offensive line for finishing blocks and pushing the pile. He still said the line has to raise its level when there isn't a back who makes defenders miss.

The defense has played outstanding football for two straight weeks, and the three takeaways were huge. Johnson called the second half a team effort, praised the game plan, and named no individual standouts.
He described the two-point play as an old Mike Martz 'sucker sneak' that worked because the defense stemmed late.
Only five penalties made it the team's cleanest game so far.
Johnson said the clock at the end of the first half was close to zero and that he'd need to rewatch the play.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 29th, 2026
headline: Elgton Jenkins is in concussion protocol on a short week ahead of Thursday night at Pittsburgh, and Monken said the backup plan is ready. Tylan Wallace's injury update is still pending, and Deshaun Watson's legs will stay organic rather than becoming a bigger designed-run plan.
summary: Monken opened by addressing the O-line: Elgton Jenkins is in the concussion protocol, and with a short week it is uncertain he can return, so the team would turn to Whip, with Parker anticipated as the backup. He framed the Thursday-night game at Pittsburgh as a mad rush for game planning but welcomed prime time, and he praised Pittsburgh's defense under a new staff as difficult to prepare for. Practice this week is mostly walk-through and jog-through with some full-speed work, with the focus on getting bodies back after a physical, intense Sunday. On Deshaun Watson, he said he's fine with the current amount of designed running, since much of Watson's rushing production came organically off scrambles. He said Watson still needs to trust his drop and eyes, and that the offense has a ways to go. He described the rookie receivers (the transcript says Casey and Denzel, likely KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston) as intelligent and diligent, but said moving them around to different spots has been counterproductive while they're still learning the nuances. He owned the offense's mistakes and penalties in a new system and said the operation, not the practice regimen, needs to be cleaner. He also praised Jared Verse's pass-rush performance and Denzel Ward's consistent high-level play, and said Tylan Wallace has no update yet while the team waits on a few things.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “I’m Better Than That” | Press Conference
headline: Schottenheimer owns the late-game blunders in the Baltimore loss; Jaishawn Barham is holding the MIKE job, Jalen Thompson is out 4+ weeks, and Tyler Smith could return for Tampa.
summary: Schottenheimer took full responsibility for the final 28 seconds in Brazil. He said he over-coached Dak Prescott on third down with a word that pushed Prescott into a conservative mindset, and that this bled into his decision on the kickoff. He stressed that he still trusts Dak completely and that he and Jerry Jones are aligned. He also said communication with Ryan Peter on game management needs to be better. Defensively he praised the inside run defense and third-down work, but criticized edge contain, sloppy tackling and the lack of a pass rush. The defense is banged up: Jonathan Bullard is out a couple of weeks with a calf strain, Jalen Thompson is out at least four weeks (likely IR-designated to return), and Cobie Durant probably will not be ready for the Thursday game against Houston. Von Miller, DeMarvion Overshown and Malik Hooker are trending toward practice. Jaishawn Barham is making a strong case to keep the linebacker spot. Both Tyler Goodson and Emari Demercado will keep competing at RB, and Tyler Smith is first in line to return after this game, potentially for Tampa. The team may sign a few players from a workout because of the injuries.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Sept 28 | Press Conference
headline: De'Von Achane is out for the season with an injury (surgery pending), and Hafley says Miami will use a committee of Ollie Gordon II, Malik Washington and DJ Herman, with Jaylen Wright day-to-day.
summary: Hafley opened by saying his heart breaks for De'Von Achane, who he expects to return strong, and said the surgery date should be known Tuesday. For the backfield, he said everyone must step up and that the backs will each have defined roles, with touches varying week to week (e.g. 8 for one back, 10 for another) and different players possibly starting drives. He praised Ollie Gordon's physical running, Malik Washington's work in a role OC Bobby Slowik had planned for him, and DJ Herman's third-down work and pass protection. Jaylen Wright, who was doubtful and held out, is day-to-day, as is Caleb Douglas, with both to be evaluated for Wednesday practice. Hafley insisted the run-first philosophy stays, citing a strong offensive line and the team's success running against Kansas City, and said no decision has been made on an outside signing. On defense he lauded Jordan Phillips for setting the edge, and said Dante Trader and Michael Taaffe will keep starting at safety for communication. Penalties (the Chop Robinson roughing call, a pre-snap penalty and an illegal contact call on Taaffe) were a major frustration, and Malik Willis was said to have improved his decision-making but needs to work on ball security.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 28, 2026
headline: Sirianni owned a sloppy loss to Chicago with no injury update on Jalen Hurts after his brief exit. The offense stalled off-schedule, turnovers piled up, and the short passing game is still broken.
summary: Sirianni took blame for a team-wide loss, saying nobody coached or played well and that the team wasn't ready. He admitted he should have gone for it on fourth-and-one, where the team instead tried to draw Chicago offside and took a penalty. He liked the later fourth-and-five attempt in hindsight. He said the coaching staff gets no information while Jalen Hurts is being evaluated, so he couldn't plan around it, and he called the first-and-goal sequence at the one (lost yards, then an interception) unfortunate. He said the second-half offense stalled because of negative plays, penalties and being off schedule in second and third-and-long, even though the run game worked in the first half. He admitted the short-of-the-line passes (screens, swings, bubbles) haven't worked, blaming number counts, missed blocks and coaching. He said the team is minus-7 in turnover differential and that this has to change. He also regretted his sideline emotion after Hurts was hit, and gave Chicago credit for outcoaching and outplaying Philadelphia.

injuries.detail: Briefly left the game and was evaluated. Sirianni gave no information on his condition and said the staff gets no info during the evaluation. He didn't mention any ongoing issue.

signals.note: Hurts left briefly for evaluation and there was no postgame update, so monitor his practice status this week.
signals.quote: I get nothing.

signals.claim: The offense had a poor game, including a red-zone interception at the one-yard line, and Hurts was part of the turnover problems.
signals.note: The turnovers and stalled red-zone work hurt his fantasy output, and the staff is reviewing play calls.

topics.detail: Sirianni said he should have gone for it on fourth-and-one. The team tried to get Chicago to jump and took the penalty, and he wants that decision back. He liked going for it on fourth-and-five.
Negative plays, a hold and penalties left the offense off schedule in the second half. Short passes (screens, swings, bubbles) have not worked, because of number counts and missed blocks.
The team is minus-7 on the season and lost the turnover battle 3-0 in this game. Sirianni said the team will keep drilling the process and has to change it.
With 19 seconds left before halftime, the team ran a screen play that produced a touchdown. Sirianni said he trusted the quarterback's decision there.
Sirianni said he let his emotions get the best of him after a hit on Hurts on the sideline and regrets how he handled it.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Sept. 29)
headline: Short week at Cleveland: McCarthy is cutting offensive volume, hopes a returning player (first name 'Joey') can play, and expects everyone to be available Thursday.
summary: McCarthy spoke on the short week before Thursday night's game at Cleveland. A player he called "Joey" was listed as a full participant for the first time. McCarthy said he hopes the player plays, but the decision depends on how he looks Thursday's practice, and he would not commit to a pitch count. He said the information he got that morning was that everyone is making progress, and he hopes to have everybody Thursday. On offense, he calls himself the "volume police" and prefers less volume with more creativity. The unit has little experience together, and he does not want to do "a bunch of things not so well." He said the early struggles were on third down in weeks one and two. First-down production and third-down production both improved last week, and the team hasn't topped 70 plays in a game yet. He praised the first-year lineman's poise and said the game plan will protect the pre-snap operation in what he expects to be a loud Cleveland environment. He called Aaron Rodgers a key asset for handling that noise because of his road and prime-time experience, and he expects a physical AFC North game.

injuries.detail: Listed as a full participant for the first time. McCarthy hopes he plays but would not commit, and he would not say whether there would be a pitch count. Tomorrow is the first full-speed practice and the decisions will follow from it.

signals.claim: Rodgers will lead the offense's handling of crowd noise at Cleveland on Thursday night.
signals.note: The offense is deliberately limiting volume on a short week, so expect a streamlined game plan built around Rodgers' experience rather than a wide-open script.
signals.quote: a key asset for us as far as how we'll operate in the noise

signals.claim: The offense will shape its pre-snap operation around the first-year player's limited experience in the loud Cleveland environment.
signals.note: The offensive line is leaning on a first-year player, so the pre-snap operation and pass protection are worth watching in a hostile stadium.
signals.quote: he's a powerful man

topics.detail: McCarthy favors less volume and more creativity, and he acts as the "volume police." He said cutting back doesn't mean only basic formations. Because the offense lacks experience together, he wants a small number of things done well. The offense hasn't run 70 plays in a game yet.

The early-season problem was third down in weeks one and two, which limited first- and second-down chances. Both first- and third-down production improved last week. McCarthy credited the explosive plays from under center to working through the playbook menu.

McCarthy said moving a corner who has mostly practiced outside into the slot is possible. He said matchups drive personnel groups and that the team has played different combinations since camp. He wouldn't say how the returning player would change the defense, saying it would have to wait for the game.

The team practices later in the day, which gives players more sleep and recovery time and lets coaches finish the game plan, since this practice combines Thursday and Friday work. It is more of a jog-through pace.

McCarthy expects a loud environment and a physical, "knock down drag out" game in Cleveland. He described last Sunday's game as typical AFC North football. He said he is happy to see Deshaun Watson healthy and playing well.
